analysis: Point Process Model Scoping — Covariate Inventory
template_paper: Bilotti, Kempf, Oksanen, Scholtus & Nakoinz (2024) PLOS ONE 10.1371/journal.pone.0297931

template_method.null_model: CSR (homogeneous Poisson), then inhomogeneous Poisson with covariates
template_method.model_fitting: ppm() in spatstat (R) — log-linear intensity as function of covariates
template_method.clustering_tests: K, L, PCF, G, F functions with 999 MC CSR envelopes
template_method.site_types: Separate patterns for settlements vs funerary/ceremonial

our_approach.key_test: Fit Model A (intensity ~ covariates) vs Model B (intensity ~ covariates + GC_distance). LRT/AIC for whether GC_distance improves monument fit but NOT settlement fit.
our_approach.observation_window: Global land surface (custom owin from Natural Earth coastlines)

elevation_m.status: READY — already used in ML feature importance analysis

dist_to_coast_km.status: READY — already used in ML feature importance

dist_to_river_km.status: READY — already used in ML feature importance

seismic_pga.status: AVAILABLE — used in ML feature importance, check if file still exists

cloud_cover.status: AVAILABLE — used in ML feature importance, check if file still exists

slope_degrees.status: COMPUTE — can derive from existing ETOPO1 using numpy gradient

precipitation_mm.source: WorldClim v2.1 or CHELSA (mean annual precipitation)

agricultural_suitability.source: GAEZ v4 (FAO/IIASA) or already have agricultural_suitability.npy
agricultural_suitability.status: CHECK — may already be computed, verify format

soil_type.status: NOT NEEDED for first pass — Bilotti didn't use soil either

topographic_wetness_index.status: DEFER — only useful at regional scale, not global

distance_to_water_strahler.status: DEFER — Natural Earth rivers are adequate for global scale

minimum_viable_model.test: LRT comparing Model A (without GC dist) vs Model B (with GC dist), separately for monuments and settlements

implementation_notes.python_vs_R: spatstat in R is the gold standard and what reviewers expect. But Python implementation via scipy.optimize (maximum likelihood) or pointpats package is also viable. Recommend R for the final paper figures, Python for prototyping.
implementation_notes.observation_window: For global analysis, use land polygons from Natural Earth as the observation window. For regional analysis, use continental bounding polygons.
implementation_notes.edge_correction: Use Ripley isotropic correction explicitly in Kest(). Define custom owin from land polygons.
implementation_notes.key_diagnostic: rhohat() plots showing monument intensity vs GC distance, separately for monuments and settlements. This is the money figure — if it shows a spike near 0 km for monuments but flat for settlements, the paper writes itself.
